# St. Isidore University Press (Jsidoris Euniversitatis Scriptorium)

> The St. Isidore University Press (Jsidoris Euniversitatis Scriptorium) is a heteronymous press whose faculty are listed in [about.html](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/about.html).

This is a plain-text edition of its books, one UTF-8 file per essay or section. Each file opens with a header giving the title, author, book, and the URL of the section on the site, followed by numbered blocks (¶n): one per paragraph, quoted paragraph, verse block, or list item. Cite as [1.4 ¶12] for Various Asides essay 1.4, block 12, or [hebdomad/part-iii ¶7] for the other books. The faculty are described in [About the press](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/about.txt).

## Various Asides (2026), ed. Ludovico Ambrosius

- [Foreword](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/0-3-foreword.txt): Ludovico Ambrosius
- [Somewhere, USA](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/1-1-somewhere-usa.txt): E. Lawrence Hayward; reviews Tom Turner’s A History of Somewhere on the literary trope of the fictional place
- [Knowing Falsehoods](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/1-2-knowing-falsehoods.txt): Tom G. Turner; repays the favor by reviewing Law Hayward’s Science Mythology
- [Sins of the Authors](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/1-3-sins-of-the-authors.txt): Lyzander Keretzky; considers poetic and forensic apologetics in Christian fantasy writing
- [Texan Literature Seen as a Middle School Science Fair Project](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/1-4-texan-literature-seen-as-a-middle-school-science.txt): Michael A. Seeley; argues for science fiction as the most truly Texan form of literature
- [Dying for Love of Power](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/1-5-dying-for-love-of-power.txt): Edkar Marenko; reviews the digital horrors of Zero HP Lovecraft’s They Had No Deepness of Earth
- [In Front Of The Kids](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/2-1-in-front-of-the-kids.txt): Porphyry Pterpsichore; finds in 1990s children’s cartoons a true if limited lesson about man’s natural, political, civilized, and religious nature
- [A New Birth of Liberty](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/2-2-a-new-birth-of-liberty.txt): Edkar Marenko; reads a political cartoon against its propagandist’s intentions
- [A Natural History of Film](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/2-3-a-natural-history-of-film.txt): E. Lawrence Hayward; offers a quasi-Cavellian account of film, television, animation, and CGI, with particular attention to natality
- [The Burden of Pursuit](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/2-4-the-burden-of-pursuit.txt): Hugo Purcell; pursues some themes in The Winter’s Tale
- [The Snort Came to a Stop](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/3-1-the-snort-came-to-a-stop.txt): Edkar Marenko; rereads as an adult a P.D. Eastman philological parable
- [What Is Difficult Art?](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/3-2-what-is-difficult-art.txt): Tom G. Turner; defends artistic modernism via a hostile reading of Tolstoy’s What Is Art?
- [Three Problems of Poetic Economy](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/3-3-three-problems-of-poetic-economy.txt): Hugo Purcell; queries the position of right-wing literature, the rights of genius, and the challenge of machine learning
- [A Severe Poetry](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/3-4-a-severe-poetry.txt): Michael A. Seeley; reads Vico’s New Science as a failed escape from the hermeneutic circle
- [Anarchitectonic](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/3-5-anarchitectonic.txt): Lyzander Keretzky; argues for a hero-worshipping arbitrariness as the cure for what ails the modern multiversity
- [Four Poetic Trinities](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/3-6-four-poetic-trinities.txt): Ludovico Ambrosius; write on the poetic theology of four short poems
- [When Did Jacob Marry Leah?](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/4-1-when-did-jacob-marry-leah.txt): Tom G. Turner; issue-spots Jacob’s putative marriage to Leah
- [The Letter Killeth](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/4-2-the-letter-killeth.txt): E. Lawrence Hayward; considers the letter and the American spirit of the law
- [Protest Against Protest Votes](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/4-3-protest-against-protest-votes.txt): Lyzander Keretzky; compares protest votes to frivolous lawsuits
- [Why Why Liberalism Failed Failed (Liberalism)](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/4-4-why-why-liberalism-failed-failed-liberalism.txt): Michael A. Seeley; faults Deneen’s Why Liberalism Failed for excessive liberalism
- [The Customer Is Always Right, The Manager Is Always Left](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/4-5-the-customer-is-always-right-the-manager-is.txt): Edkar Marenko; offers a feminist Marxist take on Walter Lippmann
- [Two Cheers for Oligarchy](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/4-6-two-cheers-for-oligarchy.txt): Hugo Purcell; offers a limited defense of exclusive cabals and bloodline management
- [Ten Regular Parables](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/4-7-ten-regular-parables.txt): Ludovico Ambrosius; spin out ten parables of complexity, chance, and the passage of time
- [Mirror of Clankers](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/5-1-mirror-of-clankers.txt): Michael A. Seeley; finds in Anthropic’s “Claude’s Constitution” a remarkable though flawed exercise in practical metaethics
- [Brutal Wonder](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/5-2-brutal-wonder.txt): Porphyry Pterpsichore; appraises Costin Alamariu’s Selective Breeding and the Birth of Philosophy as an endeavor more of race mythology than race science
- [The Defective Children of Zard: Or, the Kind Doctor and the Devious Chemist](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/5-3-the-defective-children-of-zard-or-the-kind.txt): Hugo Purcell; tells the history of Zard, where once, about half the children were born defective
- [Melodies Unheard](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/5-4-melodies-unheard.txt): Tom G. Turner; meditates on human life as the extension of reason over time
- [Reading? No Such Thing!](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/5-5-reading-no-such-thing.txt): Lyzander Keretzky; retreads in increasingly deranged fashion the bedrock question of whether reading exists
- [Against Some Common Notions](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/5-6-against-some-common-notions.txt): Edkar Marenko; considers how to talk about odd philosophical notions
- [Disavowals](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/6-1-disavowals.txt): Overheard in the Faculty Lounge; prepared a selection of remarks on diverse topics, drawn from the faculty lounge commonplace book
- [Report of the Committee on Written Scholarship](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/6-2-report-of-the-committee-on-written-scholarship.txt): the Committee
- [Bibliography](https://j-e-scriptorium.github.io/texts/various-asides/6-3-bibliography.txt)
